profile.campus: Leesburg, Loudoun County, Virginia (Microsoft data center presence)
profile.address: 19515 Dulles Greenway, Leesburg, Loudoun County, Virginia, 20175
profile.reading:
This building is part of Microsoft's Leesburg, Loudoun County, Virginia data center presence, one of several Northern Virginia jurisdictions, alongside Ashburn, Sterling, Manassas City, and Prince William County, where Microsoft has built out Azure infrastructure according to Bisnow's reporting on the company's regional footprint. Loudoun County's own economic development office has said data centers contributed $859 million in county tax revenue in 2025, funding schools, public safety, and parks, and that computer equipment personal property taxes from data centers, about $670.3 million in fiscal year 2025, are the county's single largest source of personal property tax revenue; Microsoft is one of the county's largest data center taxpayers alongside Amazon Web Services and Google. Microsoft has also invested directly in Loudoun County's schools and community programs, including STEM kits distributed to Loudoun Public Schools middle school students through the Loudoun Education Foundation. Data Center Frontier has covered Leesburg specifically as an emerging data center cluster still catching up in scale to the older, denser "Data Center Alley" concentration around Ashburn, though Leesburg's campus footprint, including Microsoft's, has grown substantially in recent years. Microsoft has not published this specific Leesburg building's address-level investment figure, square footage, or MW capacity, so this registry records county-wide tax and community-investment figures as regional context rather than building-specific facts.

Dominion Energy, the regional utility serving Loudoun and Prince William counties, has repeatedly cited Northern Virginia data center growth as the largest driver of new electricity demand in its Virginia service territory in filings with the Virginia State Corporation Commission, prompting new transmission and generation investment; Virginia's data center sales-and-use tax exemption, administered by the Virginia Economic Development Partnership, has been a material factor cited by state and local officials in why Microsoft and other hyperscalers have concentrated so much investment in this specific corridor rather than spreading it across lower-tax states.

reading.body:
Microsoft does not publish power capacity, square footage, or facility-specific details for individual Azure data center campuses, including this Leesburg site in Loudoun County. The company discloses only aggregate worldwide statistics covering 80+ regions and 500+ data centers globally. Without published specifications, this campus cannot be sized or ranked by its own metrics.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 have published megawatt figures totaling 1,375 MW. This Leesburg campus is one of Microsoft's Northern Virginia installations spanning multiple counties in Data Center Alley, a region also containing major facilities from AWS, Google, and Meta, but it does not appear in the state's published capacity rankings because no figure has been disclosed.

The absence of published data means this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling relative to grid constraints or regional compute density. To understand Microsoft's power footprint in Virginia or this site's contribution to US AI infrastructure, researchers depend on aggregate filings, utility reports, or third-party estimates, not operator disclosure.
